I will keep doing what I trust most here in Quzhou County: a winter wheat and summer maize rotation. That is the safest and steadiest way for me to use my land, water, and labor. I am 64, so I will not spread myself across too many crops that need more watching, more hand work, or harder selling. Wheat and maize fit our local climate, I know their field work well, and I can manage them with ordinary machines and familiar inputs. At the start of this season, my wheat is already in the ground from last autumn, so I will push for a stable wheat harvest first, then I will turn the land quickly into summer maize. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I care about stable yield and better resistance more than saving a little on seed. I will fertilize enough for yield but not excessively, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and spray only as needed for the common diseases, insects, and weeds I usually face. I will keep the system simple, practical, and low-risk because that is what I would choose for myself.
